cards.explanation: The answer is three thousand. Saul takes "…three thousand chosen men from all Israel…" and goes looking for David and his men (1 Samuel 24:2). That's a LOT of sandals on one dusty road, friends. All that marching just to find David.

The answer is David and his men, tucked back in the recesses of the cave (1 Samuel 24:3). Saul walks in, and the very men he's searching for are sitting back in the shadows. I think that's the quietest a group of grown men has ever been.

The answer is enemy. David's men say, "This is the day about which the LORD said to you, ‘Behold, I will deliver your enemy into your hand…’" (1 Samuel 24:4). Then they urge David toward Saul. I think they were ready to start the celebration.

The answer is that David cuts off a corner of Saul's robe. He "…stealthily cut off a corner of Saul’s robe." (1 Samuel 24:4). It's a small snip, and it leads to a big moment. Keep an eye on that little piece of cloth, friends, because it comes back.
The answer is False. "Afterward, David’s conscience was stricken because he had cut off the corner of Saul’s robe." (1 Samuel 24:5). He didn't feel good about it. That tells you a lot about David.
The answer is anointed. David says, "May I never lift my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed." (1 Samuel 24:6). That's the reason he gives his men, plain and simple.

The answer is True. Verse 7 says, "With these words David restrained his men, and he did not let them rise up against Saul." (1 Samuel 24:7). Those men had just said it was the day, and David still held them back. He did it with his words. Afterward, his own conscience was stricken just for cutting off the corner of Saul's robe.

The answer is that Saul leaves the cave and goes on his way. "Then Saul left the cave and went on his way." (1 Samuel 24:7). He walks out while David is holding his men back. Quiet exit, and a corner of his robe is already gone (1 Samuel 24:4). Then David gets up, goes out of the cave, and calls out to him.

The answer is that David bows facedown in reverence. First he calls out, "My lord the king!" Then David "…bowed facedown in reverence" (1 Samuel 24:8). He greets the king who has been hunting him (1 Samuel 24:11) with a bow. That tells you what's in his heart toward Saul, friends.
The answer is harm. David asks, "Why do you listen to the words of men who say, ‘Look, David intends to harm you’?" (1 Samuel 24:9). He's asking Saul to think about who he's listening to.
The answer is True. David says, "I was told to kill you, but I spared you…" (1 Samuel 24:10). He says it right to the king's face. I think that's honest about how close it got.

The answer is rebellion. David says, "Know and see that there is no evil or rebellion in my hands." (1 Samuel 24:11). Just before that he tells Saul, "…look at the corner of your robe in my hand." So the robe corner is his proof.

The answer is False. David says, "May the LORD judge between you and me, and may the LORD take vengeance on you, but my hand will never be against you." (1 Samuel 24:12). He puts it in the LORD's hands, not his own.

The answer is a dead dog and a flea. David asks, "Whom are you pursuing? A dead dog? A flea?" (1 Samuel 24:14). He's calling himself small. I've been called a lot of things in my day, friends, but never a flea.

The answer is Saul's hand. David says, "May He take notice and plead my case and deliver me from your hand." (1 Samuel 24:15). He's asking the LORD to plead his case. He's talking to Saul, so "your hand" is Saul's.
The answer is son. Saul calls back, "Is that your voice, David my son?" (1 Samuel 24:16). David said "my father," and Saul answers with "my son."

The answer is "You are more righteous than I." Saul tells David, "You are more righteous than I, for you have rewarded me with good, though I have rewarded you with evil." (1 Samuel 24:17). That's a hard thing for anyone to say out loud.

The answer is True. Saul says, "May the LORD reward you with good for what you have done for me this day." (1 Samuel 24:19). Those are his exact words to David. He's asking the LORD to reward David with good.

The answer is king. Saul says, "Now I know for sure that you will be king and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hands." (1 Samuel 24:20). He says it himself, right there in the wilderness.

The answer is not to cut off his descendants. Saul says, "…swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my descendants or wipe out my name from my father’s house." (1 Samuel 24:21). It's a request about his family line.
The answer is False. "…David gave his oath to Saul." (1 Samuel 24:22). He gave Saul what he asked for. Saul had asked for that oath in the verse before (1 Samuel 24:21).

The answer is up to the stronghold. "…Saul returned home, but David and his men went up to the stronghold." (1 Samuel 24:22). They each go their own way, friends. Saul heads home while David and his men climb up.
